ex.cn: 别太使劲拉，不然把手会脱落。

ex.en: I pulled on the rope to see if it was secure.
ex.cn: 我抻了抻绳子看看是否牢固。

ex.en: Stop pulling her hair!
ex.cn: 别揪她头发！

ex.cn: 她把他轻轻地拉到身边。

ex.cn: 把门拉上。

ex.en: Pull the plug out.
ex.cn: 把插头拔掉。

ex.en: She pulled off her boots.
ex.cn: 她脱下了靴子。

ex.en: He pulled a gun on me (= took out a gun and aimed it at me).
ex.cn: 他拔出枪来指着我。

ex.en: Pull your chair nearer the table.
ex.cn: 把你的椅子再往桌子拉近些。

ex.en: He pulled on his sweater.
ex.cn: 他套上了毛衣。

ex.en: She took his arm and pulled him along.
ex.cn: 她抓起他的胳膊，拉着他往前走。

ex.en: In this area oxen are used to pull carts.
ex.cn: 这个地区用牛拉车。

ex.cn: 把椅子再往桌子这边拉近些。

ex.en: They use oxen to pull their carts.
ex.cn: 他们用牛拉车。

ex.cn: 这麻袋太重了，提不起来。你得拖着走。

ex.en: I drew my chair closer to the fire.
ex.cn: 我把椅子向火旁拉近了点。

ex.en: a horse-drawn carriage
ex.cn: 马车

ex.en: He tried to kiss her but she pulled away.
ex.cn: 他想吻她，但她却扭开了身子。

ex.en: The dog snapped at her and she quickly pulled back her hand.
ex.cn: 那狗要咬她，她马上把手缩了回来。

ex.en: John pulled himself free and ran off.
ex.cn: 约翰脱身跑掉了。

senses.def: to open or close curtains, etc.

ex.en: Pull the curtains—it's dark outside.
ex.cn: 外边天黑了，把窗帘拉上。

ex.en: to pull a muscle/ligament/tendon
ex.cn: 扭伤肌肉／肌腱／韧带

ex.en: He injured his knee playing hockey.
ex.cn: 他打曲棍球时膝盖受了伤。

ex.en: Three people were injured in the crash.
ex.cn: 撞车事故中有三人受伤。

ex.en: 50 people were seriously wounded in the attack.
ex.cn: 这次攻击中有 50 人受重伤。

ex.cn: 你伤着自己了吗？

ex.en: Don't strain your eyes by reading in poor light.
ex.cn: 别在光线不足的地方看书把眼睛给伤了。

senses.def: to move a switch, etc. towards yourself or down in order to operate a machine or piece of equipment

ex.en: Pull the lever to start the motor.
ex.cn: 拉动手柄启动马达。

ex.en: Don't pull the trigger!
ex.cn: 别扣扳机！

senses.def: to move or make a vehicle move sideways

ex.en: The wheel is pulling to the left.
ex.cn: 方向盘正在向左打。

ex.en: She pulled the car to the right to avoid the dog.
ex.cn: 她把汽车向右一闪，好躲开那条狗。

senses.def: to work hard and use a lot of power

ex.en: The old car pulled hard as we drove slowly up the hill.
ex.cn: 老旧的汽车吃力地向前爬，把我们缓缓地拖上了山坡。

senses.def: to use oars to move a boat along

ex.en: They pulled towards the shore.
ex.cn: 他们向岸边划去。

senses.def: to attract the interest or support of sb/sth

ex.en: They pulled in huge crowds on their latest tour.
ex.cn: 最近巡回演出时，他们吸引了大批观众。

senses.def: to attract sb sexually

ex.en: He can still pull the girls.
ex.cn: 他仍然能让姑娘们着迷。

ex.en: She's hoping to pull tonight.
ex.cn: 她希望今晚风采迷人。

senses.def: to succeed in playing a trick on sb, committing a crime, etc.

ex.en: He's pulling some sort of trick on you.
ex.cn: 他在耍花招骗你呢。

senses.def: to cancel an event; to stop showing an advertisement, etc.

ex.en: The gig was pulled at the last moment.
ex.cn: 音乐会临时取消了。

senses.def: to trick sb
to have different aims that cannot be achieved together without causing problems
to play a joke on sb, usually by making them believe sth that is not true
used to show that you do not believe what sb has just said
senses.chn: （表示不相信对方的话）别打哈哈了

senses.def: to make the greatest effort possible to achieve sth
senses.chn: 竭尽全力；费九牛二虎之力

senses.def: to put an end to sb's project, a plan, etc.
to express sth less strongly than you are able to, for example to avoid upsetting or shocking sb

ex.en: Her articles certainly don't pull any punches.
ex.cn: 她的文章确实一针见血。

senses.def: to suddenly produce sth as a solution to a problem
senses.chn: 突然提出解决方法；突施妙计

senses.def: to make use of your place or status in society or at work to make sb do what you want
senses.chn: 凭借地位指使（某人）；弄权

senses.def: to take help or support away from sb suddenly
to try to improve your performance, work, behaviour, etc.

ex.en: You're going to have to pull your socks up.
ex.cn: 你可得加把劲儿了。

senses.def: to use your influence in order to get an advantage for sb
senses.chn: 凭影响（为某人）谋利益；（为某人）活动，走后门

senses.def: to control events or the actions of other people
to suddenly move from your house and go to live somewhere else
to work as hard as everyone else in a job, an activity, etc.
to try to trick sb; to hide your real actions or intentions from sb
to improve your situation yourself, without help from other people
to produce an expression on your face to show that you do not like sb/sth or in order to make sb laugh
senses.chn: （对某人）耷拉着脸，板着脸，做鬼脸

ex.cn: 你干吗板着脸？

senses.def: to start being more careful in your behaviour, especially by spending less money than before
senses.chn: 行为检点；（尤指）减少开支

senses.def: to criticize sb, or their work or ideas, very severely
senses.chn: 严厉斥责；痛斥；批评得体无完肤

senses.def: to criticize sb, or their work or ideas, very severely
senses.chn: 把某人（或其作品、观点等）批驳得体无完肤

senses.def: to move in front of sb/sth

ex.en: The cyclists were together until the bend, when Tyler pulled ahead.
ex.cn: 自行车选手们原本胶着在一起，直到转弯处泰勒才超前领先。

senses.def: to separate people or animals that are fighting
senses.chn: 分开，拉开（打斗的人或动物）

senses.def: to separate sth into pieces by pulling different parts of it in different directions
to start moving

ex.en: They waved as the bus pulled away.
ex.cn: 公共汽车开动时他们挥手告别。

senses.def: to move back from a place
to decide not to do sth that you were intending to do, because of possible problems

ex.en: Their sponsors pulled back at the last minute.
ex.cn: 他们的赞助人在最后时刻打了退堂鼓。

senses.def: to make an army move back from a place
to improve a team's position in a game

ex.en: Rangers pulled back to 4–3.
ex.cn: 流浪者队以 4:3 反败为胜。

ex.en: They pulled back a goal just before half-time.
ex.cn: 在上半场临结束时，他们扳回一球。

senses.def: to make sb less happy, healthy or successful
to destroy a building completely
to bring sb to a police station in order to ask them questions about a crime
to earn the large amount of money mentioned

ex.cn: 我估计她要赚 10 多万美元。

to move to the side of the road or to the place mentioned and stop

ex.cn: 警车发出信号，要我们驶向路边停靠。

ex.cn: 我们做成了这笔交易。

ex.cn: 我真没想到你把这事办成了。

ex.cn: 我尽量把这个念头忘掉。

senses.def: a service that allows Internet users to keep receiving the particular type of information that they describe by completing a form
senses.chn: 推送技术（用户能不断接收所选择的某类互联网信息）

senses.def: to spend a lot of money on enjoying yourself or celebrating sth
to go beyond the limits of what is allowed or thought to be possible

ex.en: He is a performer who consistently pushes the envelope of TV comedy.
ex.cn: 他是一个在电视喜剧表演中不断寻求突破的演员。

senses.def: an exercise in which you lie on your stomach and raise your body off the ground by pressing down on your hands until your arms are straight
trying hard to get what you want, especially in a way that seems rude
senses.chn: 执意强求的；死缠硬磨的

ex.en: a pushy salesman
ex.cn: 纠缠不休的推销员

senses.def: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past
senses.chn: （由于过去的成功过关）再冒一次险，继续碰运气

ex.en: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!
ex.cn: 上次没被逮住，但你不要再心存侥幸了！

senses.def: frightened to take risks
used when you are calling or talking to a cat
senses.chn: （用于唤猫或对猫说话）咪咪，猫咪

senses.def: a person's face or mouth
a child's word for a cat
the female sexual organs, especially the vulva
a child's word for a cat
a person who is kind and friendly, especially when you would not expect them to be like this
senses.chn: （尤指出人意料的）和蔼可亲的人

ex.en: He's just a pussycat really, once you get to know him.
ex.cn: 你了解他以后就会发现他实在和蔼可亲。

senses.def: to be careful or anxious about expressing your opinion in case you upset sb
a small tree with flowers in spring that are like soft fur
a spot on the skin containing pus
to move sth into a particular place or position

ex.en: Put the cases down there, please.
ex.cn: 请把箱子搁在那边。

ex.en: Did you put sugar in my coffee?
ex.cn: 你在我的咖啡里放糖了没有？

ex.en: Put your hand up if you need more paper.
ex.cn: 若有人还要纸，请举手。

senses.def: to move sth into a particular place or position using force

ex.en: He put his fist through a glass door.
ex.cn: 他用拳头砸穿了玻璃门。

senses.def: to cause sb/sth to go to a particular place

ex.en: Her family put her into a nursing home.
ex.cn: 她的家人把她送进了一家疗养院。

ex.en: It was the year the Americans put a man on the moon.
ex.cn: 那是美国人把人送上月球的那一年。

senses.def: to attach or fix sth to sth else

ex.en: We had to put new locks on all the doors.
ex.cn: 我们只好把所有的门都安上新锁。

senses.def: to write sth or make a mark on sth

ex.en: Put your name here.
ex.cn: 在这里填上姓名。

ex.en: Friday at 11? I'll put it in my diary.
ex.cn: 星期五 11 点？我要把它记在记事本里。

ex.en: I couldn't read what she had put.
ex.cn: 她写的什么我辨认不出来。

senses.def: to bring sb/sth into the state or condition mentioned

ex.en: I was put in charge of the office.
ex.cn: 他们让我负责管理这个办公室。

ex.en: The incident put her in a bad mood.
ex.cn: 这件事弄得她心情很不好。

ex.en: Put yourself in my position. What would you have done?
ex.cn: 你设身处地为我想想，你会怎么办？

ex.en: I tried to put the matter into perspective.
ex.cn: 我尽量正确评估这个问题。

ex.en: Don't go putting yourself at risk.
ex.cn: 当心不可冒什么风险。

ex.en: It was time to put their suggestion into practice.
ex.cn: 那时就该把他们的建议付诸实施了。

senses.def: to make sb/sth feel sth or be affected by sth
senses.chn: 使感觉到；使受到…的影响

ex.en: Her new job has put a great strain on her.
ex.cn: 她的新工作使她感到负担很重。

ex.en: They put pressure on her to resign.
ex.cn: 他们向她施加压力，让她自行辞职。

ex.en: It's time you put a stop to this childish behaviour.
ex.cn: 这种孩子气的行为你该收敛了。

senses.def: to give or attach a particular level of importance, trust, value, etc. to sth

ex.en: Our company puts the emphasis on quality.
ex.cn: 我们公司重视质量。

ex.en: He put a limit on the amount we could spend.
ex.cn: 他规定了我们开销的限额。

senses.def: to consider sb/sth to belong to the class or level mentioned

ex.en: I'd put her in the top rank of modern novelists.
ex.cn: 我认为她应属于一流的当代小说家。

senses.def: to express or state sth in a particular way

ex.en: She put it very tactfully.
ex.cn: 她的话说得很巧妙。

ex.en: Put simply, we accept their offer or go bankrupt.
ex.cn: 简单地说吧，我们要么接受他们的条件，要么破产。

ex.en: I was, to put it mildly, annoyed (= I was extremely angry).
ex.cn: 说得温和点儿，我相当恼火。

ex.en: He was too trusting—or, to put it another way, he had no head for business.
ex.cn: 他太轻信人了。或者换个说法，他没有商业头脑。

ex.en: The meat was— how shall I put it? —a little overdone.
ex.cn: 这肉嘛，怎么说呢，做得稍微老了点儿。

ex.en: As T.S. Eliot puts it…
ex.cn: 正如 T.S. 艾略特所说…

senses.def: to throw the shot
to have many sexual partners
senses.chn: 浪荡胡为；乱搞男女关系

senses.def: used to say that you think sb is capable of doing sth wrong, illegal, etc.
senses.chn: 我看…干得出（错的、违法的等事）

senses.def: to suggest sth to sb to see if they can argue against it

ex.en: I put it to you that you are the only person who had a motive for the crime.
ex.cn: 我跟你说白了，你是唯一有作案动机的人。

senses.def: to persuade sb to believe sth that is not true

ex.en: Don't try to put one over on me!
ex.cn: 你甭想蒙我！

senses.def: to force sb to experience sth difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: They really put me through it (= asked me difficult questions) at the interview.
ex.cn: 面试的时候，他们真把我折腾了一番。

senses.def: used when comparing or contrasting sb/sth with a group of other people or things to mean 'combined' or 'in total'
senses.chn: （用于与一组人或事物作比较）合计，总和，合起来

ex.en: Your department spent more last year than all the others put together.
ex.cn: 去年，你们部门的开支比其他所有部门合起来都多。

senses.def: used to tell sb to stop just talking about sth and actually do it, show it, etc.
senses.chn: 要么拿出实际行动来，要么就闭嘴；动点儿真格的，别光耍嘴皮子

senses.def: to tell a lot of people news, information, etc. that may be false
senses.chn: 散布，传播（不实的消息等）

ex.en: Someone's been putting it about that you plan to resign.
ex.cn: 有人传说你打算辞职。

senses.def: to communicate your ideas, feelings, etc. successfully to sb

ex.en: She's not very good at putting her views across.
ex.cn: 她不大善于表达自己的观点。

senses.def: to ignore or forget sth, usually a feeling or difference of opinion

ex.en: They decided to put aside their differences.
ex.cn: 他们决定搁置双方的分歧。

senses.def: to save sth or keep it available to use

ex.en: We put some money aside every month for our retirement.
ex.cn: 我们每月都存一些钱供退休后使用。

ex.en: I put aside half an hour every day to write my diary.
ex.cn: 我每天留出半个小时写日记。

senses.def: to calculate sb/sth to be a particular age, weight, amount, etc.

ex.en: The damage to the building is put at over $1 million.
ex.cn: 对这座建筑物造成的损坏估计超过 100 万美元。

senses.def: to send sb to prison, to a mental hospital, etc.
senses.chn: 把某人送入监狱（或精神病院等）

senses.def: to put sth in the place where it is kept because you have finished using it

ex.en: I'm just going to put the car away (= in the garage).
ex.cn: 我正打算把汽车开进车库。

senses.def: to save money to spend later

ex.en: She has a few thousand dollars put away for her retirement.
ex.cn: 她为退休生活积攒了几千美元。

senses.def: to eat or drink large quantities of sth

ex.en: He must have put away a bottle of whisky last night.
ex.cn: 昨晚他准是喝了一整瓶威士忌。

senses.def: to return sth to its usual place or to the place where it was before it was moved

ex.en: If you use something, put it back!
ex.cn: 用过的东西要放回原处！

senses.def: to move sth to a later time or date

ex.en: The meeting has been put back to next week.
ex.cn: 这次会议已延期到下周了。

senses.def: to cause sth to be delayed

ex.en: Poor trading figures put back our plans for expansion.
ex.cn: 贸易额不佳延缓了我们的扩张计划。

senses.def: to move the hands of a clock so that they show the correct earlier time

ex.en: Remember to put your clocks back tonight (= because the time has officially changed).
ex.cn: 记住今晚把时钟拨回去。

senses.def: to treat sth as more important than sth else
to try to forget about an unpleasant experience and think about the future
senses.chn: 把（不愉快的事）置于脑后

senses.def: to save money for a particular purpose

ex.en: I'm putting by part of my wages every week to buy a bike.
ex.cn: 我每个星期把一部分工资存起来准备买辆自行车。

senses.def: to land

ex.en: He put down in a field.
ex.cn: 他降落在一块田里。

senses.def: to make sb look or feel stupid, especially in front of other people
senses.chn: 使（当众）出丑；使出洋相；让某人现眼

senses.def: to stop holding sth and place it on a table, shelf, etc.

ex.en: Put that knife down before you hurt somebody!
ex.cn: 把刀子放下，别伤着人！

ex.en: It's a great book. I couldn't put it down.
ex.cn: 这本书棒极了。我是爱不释手啊。

ex.en: She put the phone down on me (= ended the call before I had finished speaking).
ex.cn: 她没等我把话说完就挂了线。

senses.def: to write sth; to make a note of sth

ex.en: The meeting's on the 22nd. Put it down in your diary.
ex.cn: 会议日期是 22 号。把它记在你的记事本里。

senses.def: to pay part of the cost of sth

ex.en: We put a 5% deposit down on the house.
ex.cn: 我们给这所房子交了 5% 的订金。

senses.def: to stop sth by force

ex.en: to put down a rebellion
ex.cn: 平定叛乱

ex.en: The military government is determined to put down all opposition.
ex.cn: 军政府决心镇压一切反对势力。

senses.def: to kill an animal, usually by giving it a drug, because it is old or sick
senses.chn: 药死（衰老或有病的动物）；人道毁灭

ex.en: We had to have our cat put down.
ex.cn: 我们只得用药结束了猫的生命。

senses.def: to put a baby to bed

ex.en: Can you be quiet—I've just put the baby down.
ex.cn: 请安静点儿，我刚把小孩哄睡着了。

senses.def: to present sth formally for discussion by a parliament or committee
senses.chn: 将…提请（议会或委员会）审议

ex.en: to put down a motion/an amendment
ex.cn: 提交一项动议／修正案

senses.def: to consider or judge sb to be a particular type of person

ex.en: I'd put them both down as retired teachers.
ex.cn: 我看他们俩都是退休教师。

senses.def: to put sb's name on a list, etc. for sth

ex.en: Put me down for three tickets for Saturday.
ex.cn: 给我登记预订三张星期六的票。

ex.en: They've put their son down for the local school.
ex.cn: 他们已经给儿子报名上当地的学校。

senses.def: to consider that sth is caused by sth

ex.en: What do you put her success down to?
ex.cn: 你认为她是靠什么成功的？

senses.def: to suggest yourself/sb as a candidate for a job or position

ex.en: Can I put you/your name forward for club secretary?
ex.cn: 我推荐你／提名你任俱乐部秘书好不好？

senses.def: to move sth to an earlier time or date

ex.en: We've put the wedding forward by one week.
ex.cn: 我们已把婚礼提前了一周。

senses.def: to move the hands of a clock to the correct later time

ex.en: Remember to put your clocks forward tonight (= because the time has officially changed).
ex.cn: 记住今晚把时钟指针往前拨。

senses.def: to suggest sth for discussion

ex.en: to put forward a suggestion
ex.cn: 提出建议

senses.def: to elect a political party to govern a country

ex.en: Who will the voters put in this time?
ex.cn: 这次选民会选谁执政呢？

senses.def: to fix equipment or furniture into position so that it can be used

ex.en: We're having a new shower put in.
ex.cn: 我们要安装新淋浴设备。

senses.def: to include sth in a letter, story, etc.
senses.chn: 把…写进（信函、故事等）；添上；插入

senses.def: to interrupt another speaker in order to say sth

ex.en: Could I put in a word?
ex.cn: 我可以插句话吗？

ex.en: 'But what about us?' he put in.
ex.cn: “那我们怎么办？” 他插嘴说。

senses.def: to officially make a claim, request, etc.

ex.en: The company has put in a claim for damages.
ex.cn: 这家公司已提出赔偿损失的要求。

senses.def: to give a performance of sth, especially one of a particular kind

ex.en: All the actors put in great performances.
ex.cn: 所有演员都表演得非常好。

senses.def: to spend a lot of time or make a lot of effort doing sth
senses.chn: 花费，耗费，投入（时间、心思等）

ex.en: She often puts in twelve hours' work a day.
ex.cn: 她时常每天工作十二个小时。

ex.en: He's putting a lot of work into improving his French.
ex.cn: 他正下功夫提高他的法语水平。

senses.def: to use or give money

ex.en: He's put all his savings into buying that house.
ex.cn: 他把所有的积蓄都用来买那所房子了。

senses.def: to enter a port

ex.en: They put in at Lagos for repairs.
ex.cn: 他们驶入拉各斯港进行维修。

senses.def: to officially ask for sth

ex.en: Are you going to put in for that job?
ex.cn: 你想申请那份工作吗？

senses.def: to enter yourself/sb/sth for a competition
to add a quality to sth

ex.en: He put as much feeling into his voice as he could.
ex.cn: 他尽可能把感情融进他的声音。

senses.def: to cancel a meeting or an arrangement that you have made with sb
senses.chn: 取消，撤销（与某人的会晤或安排）

ex.en: It's too late to put them off now.
ex.cn: 现在已来不及取消与他们的安排了。

senses.def: to make sb dislike sb/sth or not trust them/it
senses.chn: 使反感；使疏远；使不信任

ex.en: She's very clever but her manner does tend to put people off.
ex.cn: 她人很精明，但态度令人反感。

ex.en: Don't be put off by how it looks—it tastes delicious.
ex.cn: 别看外表就讨厌它，这东西味道可美哩。

senses.def: to disturb sb who is trying to give all their attention to sth that they are doing

ex.en: Don't put me off when I'm trying to concentrate.
ex.cn: 别在我要集中精神时打扰我。

ex.en: The sudden noise put her off her game.
ex.cn: 突然的嘈杂声干扰了她的比赛。

senses.def: to stop in order to allow sb to leave

ex.en: I asked the bus driver to put me off at the station.
ex.cn: 我请公共汽车司机让我在火车站下车。

senses.def: to make sb lose interest in or enthusiasm for sth/sb

ex.en: He was put off science by bad teaching.
ex.cn: 老师教得不好使他失去了对理科的兴趣。

ex.en: The accident put her off driving for life.
ex.cn: 那场事故让她一生都不想开车了。

senses.def: to change sth to a later time or date

ex.en: We've had to put off our wedding until September.
ex.cn: 我们只得把婚期推迟到九月。

ex.en: He keeps putting off going to the dentist.
ex.cn: 他把看牙医的事一拖再拖。

senses.def: to give sb the telephone so that they can talk to the person at the other end

ex.en: Hi, Dad—can you put Nicky on?
ex.cn: 你好，爸爸。你让尼基接电话好吗？

senses.def: to dress yourself in sth

ex.en: Hurry up! Put your coat on!
ex.cn: 快点！把外衣穿上！

senses.def: to apply sth to your skin, face, etc.

ex.en: She's just putting on her make-up.
ex.cn: 她正在化妆呢。

senses.def: to switch on a piece of equipment

ex.en: I'll put the kettle on for tea.
ex.cn: 我来烧壶水好沏茶。

ex.en: She put on the brakes suddenly.
ex.cn: 她突然踩了刹车。

senses.def: to make a tape, CD, DVD, etc. begin to play

ex.en: Do you mind if I put some music on?
ex.cn: 我放点音乐你不介意吧？

ex.en: He put some jazz on the stereo.
ex.cn: 他用立体声音响播放了一点爵士乐。

senses.def: to become heavier, especially by the amount mentioned

ex.en: She looks like she's put on weight.
ex.cn: 她似乎发胖了。

ex.en: He must have put on several kilos.
ex.cn: 他体重一定增加了好几公斤。

senses.def: to provide sth specially

ex.en: The city is putting on extra buses during the summer.
ex.cn: 今年夏天，这城市将额外增开公共汽车。

senses.def: to produce or present a play, a show, etc.

ex.en: The local drama club is putting on 'Macbeth'.
ex.cn: 当地的剧社正在演出《麦克白》。

senses.def: to pretend to have a particular feeling, quality, way of speaking, etc.

ex.en: He put on an American accent.
ex.cn: 他假操着一口美国腔。

ex.en: I don't think she was hurt. She was just putting it on.
ex.cn: 我想她没有受伤。她只是在装样子。

senses.def: to add an amount of money or a tax to the cost of sth
senses.chn: 在（价格等）上加某金额（或税额）

ex.en: The government has put ten pence on the price of twenty cigarettes.
ex.cn: 政府在每二十支香烟的价格上加征了十便士的税款。

senses.def: to bet money on sth

ex.en: I've never put money on a horse.
ex.cn: 我从未赌过马。

ex.en: I put £5 on him to win.
ex.cn: 我在他身上押 5 英镑赌他赢。

senses.def: to tell the police, etc. about where a criminal is or about a crime
senses.chn: 向（警方等）揭发，告发，举报

ex.en: What first put the police onto the scam?
ex.cn: 警方当初怎么得知这个骗局的？

senses.def: to tell sb about sb/sth that they may like or find useful

ex.en: Who put you onto this restaurant—it's great!
ex.cn: 谁告诉你这家餐馆的？真棒极了！

senses.def: to agree to have sex with sb
to make a special effort to do sth for sb

ex.en: Please don't put yourself out on my account.
ex.cn: 请别特意为我费事了。

senses.def: to cause sb trouble, extra work, etc.
senses.chn: 给某人添麻烦（或增加额外工作等）

ex.en: I hope our arriving late didn't put them out.
ex.cn: 但愿我们迟到没有给人家添麻烦。

senses.def: to be upset or offended

ex.en: He looked really put out.
ex.cn: 看来他真生气了。

senses.def: to make sb unconscious

ex.en: These pills should put him out for a few hours.
ex.cn: 这些药片会使他昏迷几个小时。

senses.def: to take sth out of your house and leave it, for example for sb to collect
senses.chn: 将…扔到外面；清理掉；扔掉

ex.en: to put the rubbish out
ex.cn: 倒垃圾

ex.en: to put the garbage/trash out
ex.cn: 倒垃圾

senses.def: to place sth where it will be noticed and used

ex.en: Have you put out clean towels for the guests?
ex.cn: 你为客人预备好干净毛巾没有？

senses.def: to stop sth from burning or shining

ex.en: to put out a candle/cigarette/light
ex.cn: 熄灭蜡烛／香烟／灯火

ex.en: Firefighters soon put the fire out.
ex.cn: 消防人员很快把火扑灭了。

senses.def: to produce sth, especially for sale

ex.en: The factory puts out 500 new cars a week.
ex.cn: 这家工厂每周生产 500 辆新汽车。

senses.def: to publish or broadcast sth

ex.en: Police have put out a description of the man they wish to question.
ex.cn: 警方公布了他们想要讯问的那名男子的特征。

senses.def: to give a job or task to a worker who is not your employee or to a company that is not part of your own group or organization

ex.en: A lot of the work is put out to freelancers.
ex.cn: 许多工作都外包给自由职业者了。

senses.def: to make a figure, result, etc. wrong

ex.en: The rise in interest rates put our estimates out by several thousands.
ex.cn: 利率上升使我们的估算差了好几千。

senses.def: to push a bone out of its normal position

ex.en: She fell off her horse and put her shoulder out.
ex.cn: 她落下马来，造成肩关节脱位。

senses.def: to develop or produce new leaves, shoots, etc.
to leave a port

ex.en: to put out to sea
ex.cn: 起航出海

ex.en: We put out from Liverpool.
ex.cn: 我们从利物浦起航。

senses.def: to continue with and complete a plan, programme, etc.

ex.en: We managed to put the deal through.
ex.cn: 我们设法做成了这笔生意。

senses.def: to make sb experience sth very difficult or unpleasant

ex.en: You have put your family through a lot recently.
ex.cn: 最近你让家人受了不少苦。

senses.def: to arrange or pay for sb to attend a school, college, etc.
